Annnnywayy friends cat clawed the shit out of my leather couch. How do I go about telling him he needs to pay for the damages? I don't want to be a dick about it, but I feel like its enough of an issue to warrant me talking to him.

EDIT: Sorry for the confusion. I was paying rent while I was not there. And I told him to have the movers put all my stuff into my room while I was gone. The couch had been left out in the living room.
What is the best way to confront someone about damages to your property without being a dick?

You really have to take into account the trade-offs. Remember, he let you store his stuff at his place, you will possibly be future roommates, he only clawed the couch (sucks but damage could've been worse). Know that you could potentially make a hostile living arrangement if you piss him off. Besides that, there's no real great way to bring it up. Probably as casually as possible mention it and hope he offers to pay?

Just say you want him to pay for it since he didn't take care if your stuff like he should have. Try to keep a very calm voice and listen to his side of the story too. Good luck it's hard to get friends to pay for shit.

If he's an actual friend you can sit down with him and discuss grievances. If he denies fault or doesn't want to talk about it, it probably won't turn into a desirable living situation anyway. It's not even about being a dick, it's about standing up for yourself and your property. I had a roomate that was verbally abusive and walked all over me and as a twenty something male it was hard to acknowledge the fact that I was unable to stand up for myself. I thought I wanted to be the better person and didn't want it to escalate but the best thing I did was confront the situation. Might have gone on a tangent there but I think we would need to know the agreement you had with him beforehand.

Were you paying rent at the time? If not, it's hard to justify asking for money for damage incurred during free storage.

Also, if he warned you about the cat you'll sound like a dick.

If you were paying rent, and he didn't say hey my cat may trash your things, just be forthright with him. "The couch was a nice couch and I have pride in the nice things I own. I feel as though you're responsible for the damage your cat caused." Etc, etc

If I were in that situation, it would just kind of awkwardly bring it up.

"Hey man... you know... that couch was a lot of money... and it's worth less with cat scratches on it... ya know?"
"Well you left your shit at my house for month knowing I had a cat so how about my storage fee is equal to your damages?"
"Hey man, let's not break anymore thing, cool?"

Say "Hey man, my couch is ruined. I figure you can either buy it from me for $$$ or pay me $$ for the damages and I'll keep it. Tell me which way you want to go and I'll simply subtract it from next month's rent".

This will work because:

1) you kept the conversation short

2) you gave him the choice of pay a lot or pay a little, not pay or don't pay

3) the default is for him to pay. Even if he refuses to choose you simply assume he wants to only pay for the damages and take that out of next month's check (be sure to note that expense on the actual check).

To me this is a gray area. Ideally he should pay for the damage, knowing animals are unpredictable, but the reality is, money is tight for many people. But you also knew he had a cat, and animals are unpredictable. Since you were paying rent, the couch really was your responsibility in the end. You can always ask for him to pay half, but I wouldn't press it and lose the friendship, if he's that good of a friend.

Next time don't store your stuff with animals.

And I told him to have the movers put all my stuff into my room while I was gone. The couch had been left out in the living room.

Never trust someone else to take care of stuff for you. An expensive lesson to learn. If it's that important for him to pay damages, it's important enough for you to do it yourself.

Anyway, used leather couches don't sell for much anyway because most people don't know how to take care of them properly. They get dried and cracked anyway.
